title: Statistics
notes: This chapter is entirely about grouped (class-interval) data -- finding mean, mode, and median from frequency distribution tables.

Three methods to find MEAN: Direct Method (mean = sum(fi*xi)/sum(fi), xi=class mark), Assumed Mean Method (use a deviation di=xi-a to simplify arithmetic), Step Deviation Method (further simplify using ui=di/h when class widths are equal). All three give the SAME answer -- pick based on how large/messy the numbers are.
Class mark (xi) = (upper limit + lower limit)/2 for each class -- always compute this first for mean calculations.
MODE for grouped data: identify the modal class (class with highest frequency), then apply the mode formula using that class's boundaries and the frequencies of the classes right before/after it.
MEDIAN for grouped data: build a cumulative frequency (less than type) column, find n/2, locate the median class (where cumulative frequency first exceeds n/2), then apply the median formula.
Empirical relationship (approximation, not exact): Mode = 3(Median) - 2(Mean). Useful for finding one measure if the other two are known.

Word problems disguise themselves as everyday data: heartbeats, wages, electricity units, ages, literacy rates, plant counts -- always start by identifying class marks / cumulative frequencies before applying any formula.

formulas.name: Mean (Direct Method)
formulas.use: Basic mean formula using class marks xi and frequencies fi.

formulas.name: Mean (Assumed Mean Method)
formulas.formula: Mean = a + [sum(fi*di)/sum(fi)], where di = xi - a
formulas.use: When class marks are large numbers, pick a convenient assumed mean 'a' to simplify.

formulas.name: Mean (Step Deviation Method)
formulas.use: Further simplification when class width h is constant.

formulas.name: Mode of Grouped Data
formulas.use: l=lower limit of modal class, f1=modal class freq, f0=preceding class freq, f2=succeeding class freq, h=class width.

formulas.name: Median of Grouped Data
formulas.use: l=lower limit of median class, n=total frequency, cf=cumulative freq before median class, f=median class freq, h=class width.

formulas.name: Empirical Relationship
formulas.use: Quick cross-check or find a missing measure of central tendency.

examples.question: Wickets taken by a bowler in 10 matches: 2,6,4,5,0,2,1,3,2,3. Find the mode.
examples.solution: Frequency table shows 2 wickets occurred 3 times -- the maximum. So mode = 2.

exercises.question: Find the mean number of plants per house from a grouped frequency table of 20 houses (class intervals 0-2 through 12-14).
exercises.answer: 8.1 plants (Direct Method used since xi and fi values are small)

exercises.question: Find the mean daily wages of 50 factory workers from a grouped frequency table (class intervals 500-520 through 580-600).
